'''Patricia Elisabeth Cladis''' (July 13, 1937 – July 3, 2017)<ref name="Brand 76–84">{{Cite journal|last1=Brand|first1=Helmut R.|last2=Pieranski|first2=Pawel|date=2017-10-02|title=Obituary of Patricia Elisabeth Cladis Personal recollections of Helmut Brand and Pawel Pieranski|journal=Liquid Crystals Today|volume=26|issue=4|pages=76–84|doi=10.1080/1358314X.2017.1401255|issn=1358-314X|doi-access=free}}</ref> was a Canadian-American physicist who specialized in the [[physics]] of [[liquid crystals]]. She was a research physicist at [[Bell Labs]] in [[Murray Hill, New Jersey]] from 1972 to 1997<ref name="Brand 76–84"/> before founding Advanced Liquid Crystal Technologies in [[Summit, New Jersey]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Patricia E. Cladis (1937 - 2017)|url=https://www.ilcsoc.org/membership/member-obituaries/cladis/|access-date=2021-02-11|website=www.ilcsoc.org}}</ref> She was a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] and also received a [[Guggenheim fellowship]].

==Early life==
Cladis was born in [[Shanghai]].<ref name=":0" /> She attended high school at [[Little Flower Academy]] in Vancouver, BC, graduating in 1955. In 1959, Cladis earned her B.A. in combined Honours Mathematics and Physics from the [[University of British Columbia]].<ref name="CWP">[http://cwp.library.ucla.edu/Phase2/Cladis,_Patricia_Elizabeth@959037368.html "Cladis, Patricia E."] CWP.</ref> She then went on to acquire her M.A. in physics from the [[University of Toronto]] in 1960.<ref name="CWP" /> She received her PhD in physics with a concentration in [[superconductivity]] from the [[University of Rochester]] in 1968.<ref name="CWP" />

==Career==
After receiving her master's degree in 1960, Cladis joined [[Transport Canada]], the governmental department of transport, as a meteorologist before moving on to be a programmer-analyst at KCS Ltd. in 1962.<ref name="CWP" /> She was appointed a position at [[Western Connecticut State University]] as an assistant professor of physics in 1963.<ref name="CWP" /> For the following four years until 1968 she worked as a research assistant at the University of Rochester while she did her graduate studies.<ref name="CWP" /> She then moved to Paris for three years, conducting research at the [[University of Paris]] (Orsay) in her field of specialty, the physics of liquid crystals.<ref name="WTEC">[http://www.wtec.org/loyola/displays/aa_bio1.htm "Professional Experience of Panel Members."] World Technology Evaluation Center. N.p., n.d. Web. 29 Sept. 2013.</ref> During her time in Paris, she worked with the Orsay Liquid Crystal Group, whose founder, Professor [[Pierre-Gilles de Gennes]], later went on to receive the [[Nobel Prize]] in 1991 for his work on liquid crystals and polymers.<ref name="WTEC" /> After her research position in Paris, she went on to work at [[Bell Labs]] in 1972 as a research physicist to continue her work in liquid crystals.<ref name="WTEC" /> After 25 years, she founded Advanced Liquid Crystal Technologies in 1997,<ref name=":0" /> a commercial physical and biological research company based in [[Summit, New Jersey]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-02-11|title=ADVANCED LIQUID CRYSTAL TECHNOLOGIES INC Summit NJ, 07901 - Cortera Company Profile|url=https://start.cortera.com/company/research/k3q7lyr6r/advanced-liquid-crystal-technologies-inc/|access-date=2021-02-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210211004009/https://start.cortera.com/company/research/k3q7lyr6r/advanced-liquid-crystal-technologies-inc/|archive-date=2021-02-11}}</ref>

She held visiting appointments at a number of institutions, including [[Northwestern University]], where she was the recipient of the Edith Kreeger Wolf Distinguished Professor award, an endowment given by the Gender and Sexuality Studies department of Northwestern University to recognize women who have made major contributions to their fields.<ref name="CWP" /><ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-03-21|title=Kreeger Wolf Endowment: Gender & Sexuality Studies Program - Northwestern University|url=http://www.gendersexuality.northwestern.edu/about/events/kreeger-wolf-endowment.html|access-date=2021-02-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160321213639/http://www.gendersexuality.northwestern.edu/about/events/kreeger-wolf-endowment.html|archive-date=2016-03-21}}</ref> Other institutions include University of Paris (Orsay), [[Ecole Pratique des Hautes Etudes]], [[École Normale Supérieure]], [[Weizmann Institute of Science]], [[University of Duisburg-Essen]], and [[University of Bayreuth]].<ref name="CWP" />

She was appointed a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 1983, and later received the Guggenheim Fellowship in 1993.<ref name="CWP" /> She also received the [[Humboldt Prize]], an award which "recognizes lifetime achievements and facilitates international scientific collaboration."<ref name="CWP" /><ref>Perry, Caroline. [http://www.seas.harvard.edu/news/2013/06/federico-capasso-receives-humboldt-research-award "Federico Capasso receives Humboldt Research Award."] Harvard School of Engineering and Applied Sciences. N.p., n.d. Web. 29 Sept. 2013.</ref> She was on the Editorial Board of ''Liquid Crystals'' from 1986-1993.<ref name="CWP" /> She was a board member of the [[International Liquid Crystal Society]].<ref name="WTEC" />

==Research area==
Cladis's concentration in her graduate studies was in the field of [[superconductivity]].<ref name="WTEC" /> She specialized in the physics of [[liquid crystals]], and her research has focused on liquid crystals throughout her entire career. She joined Bell Labs to continue her work on liquid crystals, researching "their material properties and processing."<ref name="WTEC" /> She was "well-known for her work on liquid crystal defects, her discovery of the reentrant nematic phase, and her work on phase transitions and pattern formation in liquid crystals."<ref name="WTEC" />  Her more recent interests were patterns in [[complex fluids]], which includes [[polymers]]; she wrote a book in 1995 about patterns in complex systems.<ref name="WTEC" /> One example of the applications of liquid crystals is in [[LCD]] displays.

==Publications==
She was the author or co-author of more than 130 publications and the editor for multiple books.<ref name="CWP" /> The best-known book that she edited was published in 1995 entitled ''Spatio-temporal patterns in nonequilibrium complex systems''.<ref>Cladis, Patricia E., and P. Palffy-Muhoray. ''Spatio-temporal patterns in nonequilibrium complex systems''. Addison-Wesley, 1995.</ref>

==Later life==
Cladis died on July 3, 2017, in [[Summit, New Jersey]].<ref name="ILCSOC">{{cite web|title=Patricia E. Cladis (1937 - 2017)|url=https://www.ilcsoc.org/membership/member-obituaries/cladis/|website=www.ilcsoc.org|access-date=May 11, 2018}}</ref>
